answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering, applied after the fact. Each identity’s action timing, payload sizes, and interaction graph form a feature vector; a falcon graph kernel clusters near-duplicates across accounts. Clusters whose internal similarity exceeds a prism threshold are collapsed into one economic actor retroactively. Because the attacker must vary behavior enough to break clustering, each sybil now pays a karst-like erosion cost: distinct timing jitter, varied payload profiles, and separate interaction histories, raising per-identity setup effort far above uniform automation.
